what_this_is: Derived statistical properties of archived Grainger product pages, for driving a synthetic catalog generator. The raw corpus under raw/ is analysis input only and ships nowhere.

collection_constraints_observed.source: web.archive.org ONLY -- no request was sent to any distributor's own site
collection_constraints_observed.concurrency: serial, single process, 3-5s jittered between requests, escalating backoff on 429/5xx
collection_constraints_observed.capture_eras_used: 2015 and 2020 slug captures, and 2026 bare-SKU captures
collection_constraints_observed.capture_era_excluded: 2024 -- enumeration used from=2015&to=2021 and from=2025, so 2024 captures were never requested. 2024 slug captures are soft-404s served at HTTP 200.
collection_constraints_observed.validation: every page validated on CONTENT (spec table present, not-found markers absent), never on HTTP status

corpus.skus_enumerated_is_a_FLOOR_not_a_total: GRAINGER-APPROVED and DAYTON returned exactly the 4000-row request limit, so their URL counts are truncated. Every enumeration count here is a floor.

discard_verification.notfound_page_at_200: Pages served HTTP 200 whose CONTENT is a not-found page. Detected on content markers, never on status. 18 such pages were discarded.
discard_verification.no_spec_table: VERIFIED, not assumed: every one of the 54 no_spec_table discards in the 2026 era was re-opened from the saved HTML and checked. All 54 carry "techSpecs":null AND "techSpecsTable":{...,"specs":[]} -- the spec array is genuinely empty in the archived page. ZERO of them had a populated techSpecsTable.specs that the parser had missed. So these are absent data, not a parser limitation.
discard_verification.residual_parser_risk: The 2026 parser reads the "techSpecs" array. A second container, techSpecsTable.specs, exists in the same pages and was checked across all discards and found empty every time; it is NOT read by the parser, so a future capture that populates only that container would be silently missed.

priority_order_per_maintainer_reweightin: DEMOTED  DEMOTED_milling_dia_frequency.json -- dimensional series is a published standard

P2_price_census.collection_constraints_observed: the same as collection_constraints_observed above: web.archive.org only, the same user agent, serial single process, 3-5 s jittered from the end of one response to the next request, escalating backoff on 429/5xx
P2_price_census.capture_eras_used: Mostly 2015 group-page captures; some 2016, 2017 and 2020 group pages; end-mill item pages are 2020-2021 captures. Each type carries its own capture_years. Prices are nominal for their capture year and are not inflation-adjusted. Pages served as script shells with no item rows (all four ball-pein hammer group pages, two jobber-drill and two spiral-point-tap group pages among them) were discarded.
P2_price_census.raw_pages: analysis input only, under raw/ (gitignored); none ship

extension_69.collector: scripts/price_census_collect.py (rerunnable: it caches every response under raw/price_census/ and logs each request it sends to raw/price_census/requests.jsonl)
extension_69.parser: scripts/price_census_parse.py, which writes the two deep_types entries; its docstring states the rules the census method block leaves open
extension_69.source: archived Grainger product pages, as for the run above; web.archive.org ONLY -- no request was sent to any distributor's own site
extension_69.user_agent_deviation: differs from collection_constraints_observed.user_agent above: it names the project repository and carries no personal email address, so anyone can rerun the collector as committed
extension_69.concurrency: serial, single process, 3-5 s jittered from the end of one response to the next request, escalating backoff on 429/5xx
extension_69.capture_window: from=2015&to=2021, as for the run above; the latest capture in the window per URL

sources_by_type.lock_nuts_nylon_insert: product-group pages under the distributor's own label whose slug names a locknut; a page is kept when its group specs say Nylon Insert (5 of 9 fetched). Every row carries that one label, so the entry publishes no brand spread, brand price index or house-label ratio; brand_spread_same_spec says why.
sources_by_type.set_screws_hex_socket: category list pages (no group pages are archived for this type); each row gives brand, a full spec description, the shown price and the sale unit, and a cell is brand plus equal non-dimension specs. Five brands, but the only specs two brands share are nylon set screws, so the entry publishes no spread or tier figure; brand_spread_same_spec says why.

extension_69.clearance_rule: 84% of the lock-nut rows and 13.5% of the set-screw rows show a clearance price beside the regular price; they are priced at the regular price, and each entry records that share as clearance_rows_priced_at_regular
extension_69.not_used: the 4 locknut category list pages the collector also fetched: every row on them carries the same single label as the group pages, and their list markup does not pair a row's brand with its description reliably

request_accounting.earlier_probe: about 15 serial web.archive.org requests (CDX and two pages) sized the sources first; they were not logged request by request

extension_69.not_restated: pooled_endings_all_types, capture_eras and request_accounting in P2_price_census.json describe the run above only; these two entries are not folded into them
